title: Detection of Exosomal Biomarker by Electric Field-induced Release and Measurement (EFIRM)
protocol: Pipette 5 μl of Streptavidin-Coated magnetic microparticles into 495 μl of PBS buffer in a microcentrifuge tube.
Wash and resuspend the beads with 500 μl of PBS three times using a magnetic rack.
Let the tubes sit on the magnetic rack for 1 min during each wash.
Carefully remove the supernatant buffer without disturbing the beads after magnetization.
Place the tubes on a regular rack without magnets at the side.
Add 500 μl of PBS into the tubes and mix with pipette.
Put the tubes back on the magnetic rack to separate the beads from the solution.
Resuspend the beads into 490 μl of PBS buffer, placing the tube on the non-magnetized portion of the magnetic rack.
Pipet 5 μl of biotinylated mouse anti-human CD63 antibody at 1.0 mg/ml stock concentration into the mixture of beads.
Use the pipette to mix the beads and antibody in solution.
Place the microcentrifuge tubes containing bead and biotinylated antibody mixture on a sample rotator.
Set the rotator parameters for reciprocal rotation at 90° tilting for 5 sec and vibrating at 5° for 1 sec.
Rotate the sample-bead mixture tubes at these parameters for 30 min at room temperature (RT).
Remove unbound antibody after conjugation.
Place the tubes back in a magnetic rack for 5 min following rotation.
Perform three washes of beads by removing the liquid phase using a micropipette and washing with 500 µl of PBS.
Resuspend the beads in 490 µl of casein-PBS after the triple wash, placing them on the unmagnetized portion of the rack.
Label each tube with targeted sample ID.
Pipette a 10 µl sample of serum or saliva into the microcentrifuge tube.
Mix the sample and magnetic beads by pipetting several times using the pipette.
Place the tubes containing sample and anti-human CD63 antibody beads on the rotator and rotate for 2 hr at RT.
Perform a triple wash after 2 hr of rotation by magnetizing to separate beads from solution, removing liquid phase with micropipette, and resuspending beads in 500 µl of Tris-HCl buffer.
Apply a plastic well to an electrode array to prevent cross-contamination.
Use a 16-sensor electrode array with bare gold working, counter, and reference electrodes per unit.
Pipette stock reagents into a tube with ultrapure distilled water to prepare a mixture of 100 nM DNA probe, 0.3 M KCl, and 10 mM pyrrole.
Mix the solution thoroughly by vortexing.
Pipet 60 µl of the monomer-DNA probe mixture onto each gold electrode surface.
Examine the electrodes to ensure adequate coverage of all types of electrodes with the liquid mixture.
Electropolymerize the monomer-probe mixture on the electrode surface using a cyclic square wave (CSW) electric field profile.
Apply +350 mV for 9 sec, then switch immediately to +950 mV for 1 sec.
Repeat the CSW profile for 10 cycles, totaling 100 sec of applied electric field.
Rinse sensor surface 3 times with distilled water.
Dry the sensor surface with nitrogen gas to remove liquid completely.
Load 5 µl of 1 µM detector probe into 495 µl of bead-exosome complex mixture.
Mix the solution thoroughly using a pipette.
Pipette 60 µl of the probe and bead-exosome complex mixture onto a gold electrode surface with a magnet array underneath.
Apply 20 cycles of CSW electric field, each cycle consisting of 9 sec at -300 mV followed by 1 sec at +200 mV.
Wash-off unbound analytes on the electrode surface by triple rinsing with distilled water.
Dry the electrode with nitrogen gas.
Add 60 µl of anti-fluorescein antibody conjugated to horseradish peroxidase (HRP) at a 1:1,000 dilution in Casein/PBS.
Use an electric-field driven conjugation to complex anti-fluorescein HRP to the probe sandwich by applying -200 mV for 1 sec and +500 mV for 1 sec for 5 cycles to the electrode surface.
Triple wash sensor surface using distilled water.
Dry with nitrogen gas.
Add 60 µl of 3,3',5,5'-Tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) substrate.
Load this substrate on each sensor surface using a multichannel pipet.
Perform amperometric readout by measuring the electrode current at -200 mV for 60 sec using an electrochemical potentiostat capable of simultaneous measurement of 16 channels.
Inject 270 μl of the combined leptin-CRP working solution.
